lesson_title: The Where-Rule and the Who-Rule: GDP and GNI
hook_text: Your street produces MILLIONS. Half of it was never counted.
clip_script: Imagine your street counts everything it produced this year. The spaza's sales, the salon's braids, the mechanic's repairs — that's the street's GDP: what this PLACE made. But count carefully. The mechanic's R300 parts are already inside his R900 repair — count both and you've doubled. Uncle reselling his bakkie? Counted the year it was built — today it just changed hands. And here's where it gets interesting: the shop owned by the man from another town counts HERE — it stands here, employs here. That's the where-rule. But ask a different question — what did our PEOPLE earn, wherever they earned it? — and everything shifts: the daughter working in Sandton counts now; the outsider's profits ride out at closing time. That's GNI, the who-rule. And the grandmother minding four kids every day so their parents can work? Enormous value. No receipt. Never counted. The official number always undersells streets like ours — and now you know exactly how to read it.
visual_style: An aerial street view with rand values glowing above each business, doubling errors flashing red and cancelling; then the frame splitting into WHERE and WHO overlays as workers and profits cross the street's boundary; the uncounted grandmother glowing gold.
mood: Sharp, local, quietly political — statistics with a street conscience.
pacing: Brisk counting rhythm, two clean rule-shifts, tender beat on the uncounted work.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read the big numbers like an economist.
